**Dubai, UAE**: Al Sharqi Shipping, a leading UAE-based logistics service provider, has inaugurated its new integrated logistics and distribution hub at Dubai Industrial City, part of TECOM Group PJSC.
The newly launched facility represents an investment of AED 70 million and will serve customers across food and beverage, Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG), retail, hotels, restaurants, and cafés (HoReCa), quick-commerce, and manufacturing industries. It will cater to domestic demand while enhancing Al Sharqi Shipping’s regional distribution capabilities.
The new facility has a total built-up storage area of 280,000 sq. ft., 200,000 sq. ft. of open yard space, 30,000 sq. ft. of office space and a 40,000 sq. ft. basement area.

# Inside Our New 210,000 Sq. Ft. Deltaport Warehouse

 by Bill Heaney | Logistics 

Every hour a container sits is an hour of cost. Demurrage clocks, per diem charges, congested truck gates, and long drayage runs to inland warehouses all quietly erode margin on freight that has already crossed an ocean. For importers moving volume through the Pacific Gateway, the distance between the terminal gate and the first set of dock doors matters more than almost any other variable in the inbound supply chain.

That is exactly the gap our newest facility closes. As of August 1, 2026, 18 Wheels Warehousing and Trucking has taken possession of a 210,000 square foot distribution facility at 3995 27B Avenue in Delta (Tsawwassen), positioned directly adjacent to Deltaport, Canada's primary container terminal. It is one of the shortest drayage moves available to shippers arriving through Metro Vancouver, and it is now part of our national network.

# ID Logistics opens distribution center in Lower Saxony

 Sep 14, 2026 at 10:34 AM 

 

ID Logistics opened a new distribution center for heavy and bulky goods in the Middle Weser Park in Lower Saxony on September 12. With this expansion of XL contract logistics, the company is responding to the increasing demand in this segment.

### New Fulfillment Center in Lower Saxony

The new fulfillment center covers an area of 35,000 m² and has space for up to 7,000 items, which have special dimensions and weights of up to 180 kilograms. The center supports two logistics models: Online orders can be made ready for shipment within two hours, while in cross-docking, goods can be reloaded without storage within a maximum of four hours. ID Logistics reports a high demand for the cross-docking model.

With the opening of the new location, the area managed by ID Logistics Germany in XL contract logistics increases to over 100,000 m². The company’s logistics network extends from Lower Saxony through the Frankfurt area to southern Germany.
